speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a limp and localized pain; do you have a history of recent trauma to your leg, or does the pain occur only when you run and jump?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the pain is in the left knee but the child favors that leg, can you point to the exact spot that hurts when you press on it? Also, has he recently had a fever or noticed any swelling in his knee or hip?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE).

The presentation of a limp and referred knee pain in an overweight or developmentally typical child, where the hip is the actual source of the issue despite the pain being felt at the knee, is highly characteristic of SCFE. I need to confirm the hip exam findings.
